title: AI App Helps Tokyo Singles Find Love and Marriage
paragraphs: Japan has one of the lowest birth rates in the world, and the number of marriages has also fallen in recent decades. To help, the Tokyo city government has created its own dating app that uses artificial intelligence, and it says the app is starting to show results.

The app is called TOKYO Enmusubi, and it was launched in September 2024. Before the launch, a government survey found that about 70% of people who were interested in getting married were not actively looking for a partner.

To join the app, people have to prove that they are legally single and pass an online interview. The app is a local government program, not a business. It uses AI to suggest possible partners, and it shows users how compatible they are with each person in three levels.

According to the Tokyo government, about 36,000 people had applied to use the app by June 30, 2026. Of these, 16,000 were accepted as members. So far, 760 couples have started serious relationships, and 265 couples have married.

Some users have shared their stories. One woman said she tried the app "as a last chance" as she was getting close to her 40th birthday. After several dates, she met the man who is now her husband. A man said that the AI rated his compatibility with his girlfriend as perfect.

However, the app is only a small part of a much bigger problem. In 2025, the number of babies born to Japanese people fell for the 10th year in a row, to a record low of 671,236. The fertility rate, which is the average number of children a woman has, fell to 1.14. At the same time, about 1.6 million people died.
Some critics have also questioned whether the government should spend public money on another dating app.
